nodes.title: Basic Arithmetic
nodes.definition_plain: Addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of numbers.

sources.quote: Numbers can be added, subtracted, multiplied and divided.

nodes.title: Inverse Operations
nodes.definition_plain: Operations that undo each other, such as addition and subtraction.

sources.quote: Addition and subtraction are inverse operations.

nodes.title: Linear Equations
nodes.definition_plain: Equations of the form ax + b = c, solved by isolating the variable.

sources.quote: A linear equation has the form ax + b = c.

nodes.title: Algebra Basics
nodes.definition_plain: The foundational unit covering variables, expressions and equations.

nodes.title: Solve 2x + 4 = 10
nodes.definition_plain: A worked example: subtract 4 from both sides, then divide by 2.

nodes.title: Variables on Both Sides
nodes.definition_plain: Equations with the variable appearing on both sides, e.g. 2x + 3 = x + 7.

nodes.title: Solving by Balancing
nodes.definition_plain: Framing equation-solving as keeping both sides of a balance equal.

sources.quote: Think of the equation as a balance scale.

nodes.title: Order of Operations
nodes.definition_plain: The order in which operations are evaluated: parentheses, exponents, multiplication/division, addition/subtraction.

sources.quote: PEMDAS gives the order of operations.
